admission.justification: Reading the repaired defect as the norm would license direct staging and trust in polluted baselines; the corrected statement keeps the validated no-touch behavior (private discard, real preservation, named error) as the durable norm, so the costly mistake cannot be reintroduced as intent.

applicability: Converted memory baseline adoptions that stage, validate and commit memory content through the owned prepare/stage/validate interval.
conditions: The worktree index is reachable for copying, or absent so the private file stages empty.
The knowledge validator is bound in the adopting process; where it is not, adoption refuses.
exclusions: Unconverted adoptions, which keep the direct stage-and-commit path.
Files outside the owned interval: only the prepared ignore line is ever given back, never caller or external content.

evidence: notes/reports/l44-memory-review-M1/frozen/memory/knowledge/invariants/INV-DZB7MC-an-exception-during-staged-tree-validation.json:32 states "An exception during staged-tree validation exits a dry run with the staged index still installed." statement: During prepare/stage/validate against a private staging index, a validation exception exits with the real index untouched: staged private content is discarded, owned ignore-file bytes and mode are restored, and the named error propagates.
